message.content:
Based on the search results, here's a comprehensive guide on what medications and remedies to use when you have a cold:

## Important First Points

- **There is no cure for the common cold** – it's caused by viruses, so antibiotics won't work
- Most colds get better on their own within **7-10 days** (though coughs may last longer)
- Colds are caused by viruses, so **antibiotics are not effective** and should not be used

## Over-the-Counter Medications for Adults

### Pain Relievers / Fever Reducers
- **Acetaminophen (Tylenol)** – helps reduce fever, sore throat, headache, and muscle aches
- **Ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin)** – reduces fever, inflammation, and pain
- **Paracetamol** (in countries outside the US) – similar to acetaminophen

### For Nasal Congestion
- **Decongestant nasal sprays or drops** (e.g., Afrin, Neo-Synephrine) – relieve stuffy nose
  - ⚠️ **Important:** Do not use for more than **3-5 days** to avoid "rebound" congestion
- **Oral decongestants** (e.g., Sudafed/pseudoephedrine) – help with congestion and pressure

### For Cough
- **Cough syrups** – may provide temporary relief, though research shows they work no better than placebo for many people
- **Honey** – effective for relieving cough in adults and children over 1 year old
- **Throat lozenges or cough drops** – soothe sore throat (not for children under 4)

### Combination Cold Medicines
- Products like **Advil Cold and Sinus**, **Comtrex Day/Night** combine pain relievers, decongestants, and sometimes antihistamines
- ⚠️ **Be careful:** Check all ingredients to avoid accidentally taking too much of the same drug (especially acetaminophen, which can cause liver damage in overdose)

## Non-Drug Remedies

- **Rest** – essential for recovery
- **Stay hydrated** – water, juice, warm broth, tea, or warm lemon water with honey
- **Humidifier or cool mist vaporizer** – adds moisture to air and loosens congestion
- **Saline nasal spray or drops** – relieves nasal congestion safely
- **Steam inhalation** – breathe in steam from a hot shower or bowl of hot water
- **Gargle salt water** – soothes sore throat
- **Chicken soup** – can help ease congestion and provide nutrition

## What to Avoid

- **Aspirin for children and teenagers** – linked to Reye's syndrome, a rare but serious condition
- **Antibiotics** – ineffective against cold viruses
- **Giving honey to children under 12 months** – risk of botulism
- **Decongestant nasal sprays for more than 3-5 days** – causes rebound congestion
- **OTC cough/cold medicines for children under 6** – can cause serious side effects

## When to See a Doctor

- High fever lasting more than 3-4 days
- Symptoms lasting more than 10 days without improvement
- Difficulty breathing or shortness of breath
- Chest pain
- Severe vomiting
- Symptoms that improve then worsen again
- If you have chronic medical conditions (diabetes, heart/lung/kidney disease) or weakened immune system

## Special Notes

- **Antihistamines** are generally **not very effective** for cold symptoms (they work better for allergies)
- **Vitamin C, echinacea, and zinc** have mixed research results – vitamin C may slightly shorten symptoms if taken before they start; zinc may reduce cold length if taken within 24-48 hours of first symptoms, but nasal zinc products should be avoided due to risk of permanent smell loss
- **Smoking** makes cold symptoms worse and prolongs recovery

---

**Disclaimer:** This information is for general educational purposes. Always consult with a healthcare provider or pharmacist before taking medications, especially if you have existing health conditions, take other medications, are pregnant, or are giving medicine to children.

---

Sources:
1. https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/common-cold/
2. https://www.cdc.gov/common-cold/treatment/index.html
3. https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/common-cold/diagnosis-treatment/drc-20351611
4. https://www.webmd.com/cold-and-flu/head-cold-remedies-treatments
5. https://www.elmsmedicalkent.nhs.uk/media/content/files/Common%20Cold%20in%20Adults.pdf
6. https://www.webmd.com/cold-and-flu/decongestants-antihistamines-cold
